correctness.rationale: Use the stated row-player payoffs and sum over neighbors: with degree d and m cooperative neighbors the three payoffs are d(b-2c)+mc, mb, and d(b-c_I). With no cooperative neighbors I strictly wins, and if all neighbors cooperate D strictly wins. With d=2 and m=1, C beats D exactly for b>3c and beats I exactly for c_I>3c/2. With the two C ties excluded, C is never a best reply outside the simultaneous strict regime. A possible D–I tie at m=1 outside that regime does not occur in a Nash profile, since there are no cooperators. In the strict regime every C has exactly one C neighbor, and any adjacent noncooperator must be D; if it is interior it must have a second C neighbor. Induction on either side of a CC block therefore fills the whole component. This gives exactly the three labeled CCD phases on cycles with 3 dividing the order, or D(CCD)^k on paths of order 3k+1 with k>=1 because endpoints cannot be C. In either case the words satisfy the same strict local rules. No-cooperator profiles must be all I, and disjoint components contribute independent factors. The smallest allowed path and cycle respect these rules.
residual_risks: The large-order assertions in the supplied script check the predictor's output sets, not an independent best-reply enumeration at those orders. The proof, not the script, excludes any other large-ring equilibrium.

value.rationale: This natural finite-boundary question in an existing simulation model has an exact qualitative answer that local stability alone does not give: there may be no cooperative pure profile even where its local ingredients all strictly best-reply. Closing the ends changes both the order residue and the number of phases, for example P_4 has an extra profile and C_4 does not, while C_3 has three extras and P_3 none. The proof rules out hidden mixtures of separated cooperative blocks and all-individual domains. At the 10,000-agent scale used for the degree-two simulations, it distinguishes absence of a noiseless cooperative Nash state from the paper's stochastic persistence question; it does not purport to explain the positive-mutation law.
residual_risks: The contribution is an analytically short deterministic boundary classification; it supplies no stationarity, mixing, or dynamic convergence result.
